boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Pittsburgh-Pittsburgh Campus, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A calm, under-21-safe first-weekend route that begins with campus orientation points and expands into Oakland’s public cultural spaces.

cards.title: Start beneath the Cathedral arches
cards.subtitle: Friday morning · Cathedral of Learning
cards.notes: Enter the Cathedral and pause in the Commons Room to get oriented. Use the open hall as a landmark before heading to your next campus stop.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable first meeting point inside Pitt’s landmark building.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitt describes the Commons Room as a Gothic-style hall in the Cathedral of Learning used for study, contemplation, and celebration.
cards.source_title: Cathedral Commons Room — University of Pittsburgh
cards.access_notes: The source lists the location as Fifth Avenue at Bigelow; follow any posted building or event access rules.

cards.title: Look for the Nationality Rooms
cards.subtitle: Friday morning · Cathedral of Learning
cards.notes: Use the Cathedral’s first and third floors for a self-guided look at the Nationality Rooms, while respecting that they are active classrooms.
cards.short_summary: Thirty-one culturally inspired classroom spaces connect the Cathedral to Pittsburgh’s communities.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitt states that its thirty-one Nationality Room classrooms are in the Cathedral of Learning and are used as university classrooms.
cards.source_title: Nationality Rooms and Intercultural Exchange Programs — University of Pittsburgh
cards.access_notes: These are active classrooms; visit only when rooms are accessible and do not interrupt classes.

cards.title: Find the Union information desk
cards.subtitle: Friday midday · 3959 Fifth Avenue
cards.notes: Stop at the main-floor information desk and ask one practical campus question, then use the building directory to identify student services and meeting spaces.
cards.short_summary: A student-life hub in Pitt’s former Hotel Schenley.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitt identifies the William Pitt Union as home to more than 300 student organizations and places an information desk on its main floor.
cards.source_title: Student Union Services — University of Pittsburgh
cards.access_notes: The Student Unions page lists academic-year building hours of 8 a.m.–11 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and 8 a.m.–midnight Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Map a resource at O’Hara
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · 3900 O’Hara Street
cards.notes: Walk through O’Hara and note where the Writing Center and Math Assistance Center are, so you know where to return when coursework starts.
cards.short_summary: A student center that combines organization space with academic support.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitt says O’Hara Student Center houses the Math Assistance Center and Writing Center and provides meeting and activity space for student organizations.
cards.source_title: O'Hara Student Center — University of Pittsburgh
cards.access_notes: Check the current building schedule before visiting; Pitt lists varying hours by day and term.

cards.title: Make Hillman your study fallback
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · 3960 Forbes Avenue
cards.notes: Walk into Hillman, find the service desk, and identify one floor you could use for focused work when your residence hall feels too busy.
cards.short_summary: Pitt’s principal Oakland library offers study access and in-person assistance.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitt’s library system says Hillman provides reference and referral help, technology lending, and academic-year study-space access on a 24/5 schedule.
cards.source_title: Public & Access Services at Hillman — University of Pittsburgh Library System
cards.access_notes: Pitt notes that a valid Pitt ID is required for Hillman access from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m.; verify current library hours before going.

cards.title: Take a daylight pause at Schenley Plaza
cards.subtitle: Friday late afternoon · Across Fifth Avenue from the Cathedral
cards.notes: Cross at a marked intersection and use the plaza’s lawn and seating for a short reset. Keep it simple: orient yourself to the park entrance and nearby museums.
cards.short_summary: A public greenspace linking Oakland’s campus and cultural district.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitt says Schenley Plaza was revitalized with Pittsburgh Parks Conservancy construction support and is located across Fifth Avenue from the Cathedral of Learning.
cards.access_notes: Use marked crossings around the plaza and observe posted park rules and any event setup.

cards.title: Visit Heinz Chapel during visitor hours
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · South Bellefield Avenue
cards.notes: Plan a quiet daytime visit and take time with the building’s interior details. Check the chapel schedule first because private events can change access.
cards.short_summary: A nonsectarian chapel on campus with scheduled visitor hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Heinz Chapel describes itself as a nonsectarian Pitt-campus chapel and lists visitor hours Monday through Thursday from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., subject to closures.
cards.access_notes: The chapel says it may close for university holidays or private events; email the chapel office to arrange an outside-hours visit.

cards.title: Use your Pitt ID at Phipps
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · One Schenley Park
cards.notes: Bring your Pitt student ID and confirm the season before you go. Follow the conservatory route at your own pace and leave time for the public gardens.
cards.short_summary: A nearby conservatory with a Pitt student-ticket benefit in fall and spring.
cards.evidence_claim: Phipps states that Pitt students receive free student tickets during the fall and spring semesters when presenting student ID.
cards.source_title: Hours and Admission — Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens
cards.access_notes: Phipps lists regular hours and says Pitt students may visit during normal business hours without prior booking; bring student ID and verify seasonal eligibility.

cards.title: Choose an art-gallery loop
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · 4400 Forbes Avenue
cards.notes: Bring your Pitt ID, pick a few galleries rather than trying to see everything, and use the museum map to make a comfortable first visit.
cards.short_summary: An Oakland art museum offering free fall-and-spring admission to Pitt students.
cards.evidence_claim: Carnegie Museum of Art states that University of Pittsburgh students receive free admission during fall and spring semesters with a valid student ID.
cards.source_title: Come Visit — Carnegie Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Friday–Wednesday hours of 10 a.m.–5 p.m. and Thursday hours of 10 a.m.–8 p.m.; confirm the day’s schedule before traveling.

cards.title: Add the natural-history galleries
cards.subtitle: Sunday daytime · 4400 Forbes Avenue
cards.notes: Return to the shared Carnegie building with your Pitt ID and focus on one natural-history section. A short, intentional visit keeps the weekend unhurried.
cards.short_summary: A second museum experience in the Carnegie building adjacent to campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Carnegie Museum of Art states that its ticket includes access to both the Carnegie Museum of Art and Carnegie Museum of Natural History, and that Pitt students are admitted free in fall and spring with valid ID.
cards.source_title: Come Visit — Carnegie Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: The source says the museums share a building; the Pitt student admission benefit applies in fall and spring semesters with valid student ID.
